clue.text: Fabulous writer of no little note left in beautiful French town

indicators.note: no in front of the little note says that note is dropped from the writer's full name

parts.note: La Fontaine was the French author of the Fables
la is the sixth note of the sol-fa scale, a short word

indicators.note: in says the letter for left goes inside the word for beautiful

parts.note: beau is French for beautiful

explanation.surface: A renowned fabulist leaves a short note behind in a lovely French town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fabulous' suggests marvellous but means writer of fables. 'no' removes the little note from his name; 'in' places the letter for left inside the French adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Fontainebleau is a town south-east of Paris famous for its château and forest.

clue.text: Serviceman's note book containing frivolous material

annotationWithheld.why: Serviceman's note book containing frivolous material (6,8): F + LIGHT + SERGE + NT accounts for all but the A of SERGEANT, which no clue word supplies; scan confirms the clue as held
annotationWithheld.clue: Serviceman's note book containing frivolous material

clue.text: American city writer climbing in the Himalayas

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means the pieces read upwards, so the run is turned backwards

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles
a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: Someone from an American city goes up into the mountains to write.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' in a down clue sends the city plus writer upwards, so they read backwards in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Nepal is the kingdom lying along the Himalayan range, so it is found in those mountains.

clue.text: To a shopper, oddly enough, it may indicate possession

indicators.note: oddly enough suggests the letters of the phrase are set out in a strange new order

explanation.surface: A remark to a customer that something might show who owns what.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of TO A SHOPPER, rearranged ('oddly enough'), give the punctuation mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The raised comma marks the possessive, as in a cat's whisker.

clue.text: Harmful report about doctor's inversion

indicators.note: about says the word for report is placed around the other piece

parts.note: a report is a loud noise, as of a gun

indicators.note: inversion tells us the doctor's abbreviation is turned upside down

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor

explanation.surface: A damaging account of a physician turning things on their head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inversion' turns the doctor's two letters round, and 'about' wraps the report around them.
explanation.definitionFit: Noisome means offensive or injurious, especially of smells, so harmful fits.

clue.text: Damned fortunate!

definitions.meaning: used as a mild oath, as in 'the ... thing won't start', a euphemism for cursed

explanation.definitionFit: The word serves both as a polite swearword and as a word for lucky or holy.

clue.text: Bring in a vessel, by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it says the word for a vessel is heard rather than written

parts.note: an urn is a vase or container

explanation.surface: Bringing a vase or a ship into port, so it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: URN, said aloud in a non-rhotic British accent, matches the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring in money is to make it as wages or profit.

clue.text: Guarantee subject to money received in America.

parts.note: under means subject to, as under orders
in US usage the take is the money taken in, the takings

explanation.surface: A promise made dependent on cash coming in across the Atlantic.
explanation.definitionFit: To undertake is to pledge or promise, the same as to guarantee something.

clue.text: Catch connection and make the game

parts.note: to contract an illness is to catch it
a bridge connects two places

explanation.surface: A tip for winning: grab the link and the match is made.
explanation.definitionFit: Contract bridge is the standard modern card game of bidding and tricks.

clue.text: To speak off the cuff one's better without it

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the word for better goes outside it, the one's

parts.note: to better something is to improve it
one is I, and the 's stands for is, so the two together give IS

explanation.surface: Advice that unscripted speakers do better without notes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is the old sense of outside: the word for better sits outside 'it', meaning the one's piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To improvise is to perform or speak without preparation.

clue.text: Send a message to a daughter in port

indicators.note: in says the article and the daughter's letter go inside the port

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian port
D is the abbreviation for daughter in genealogies

explanation.surface: Contacting a girl who is staying in a harbour town.
explanation.definitionFit: To radio someone is to transmit a message to them by wireless.

clue.text: Governor linked with fate of a serf

parts.note: HE, His Excellency, is the title given to a colonial governor
one's lot is one's destiny

explanation.surface: A ruler bound up with the destiny of a peasant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of a' links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Helots were the state-owned serfs of ancient Sparta.

clue.text: About to leave seashore, hops in here to dry

indicators.note: to leave says the abbreviation for about departs from the seashore word

parts.note: the coast is the shore of the sea
C, for circa, means about

explanation.surface: Someone about to quit the beach while hops go in to be dried.
explanation.walkthrough: COAST loses C ('About ... to leave'). An oast is a kiln for drying hops, typical of Kent in England.
explanation.definitionFit: An oast house is the kiln where harvested hops are dried.

clue.text: It's served with ratatouille, primarily, and wine

indicators.note: primarily picks out the opening letter of the vegetable dish

parts.note: It is Italian vermouth, as in the cocktail gin and it

explanation.surface: A dish brought with ratatouille and a glass of wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's served' looks like food but is the definition: a summons is served on someone. IT for Italian vermouth is a crossword convention from 'gin and it'.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal summons or court order is formally delivered, or served, on its recipient.

clue.text: It may be broken by colonel stumbling round strange bar

indicators.note: round says the jumbled officer goes around the other jumbled piece
stumbling suggests the officer's letters lurch into a different order
strange signals that the three letters of the word bar are rearranged

explanation.surface: An officer trips over a peculiar counter and breaks something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stumbling' scrambles the officer's seven letters, 'strange' the three of the counter, and 'round' sets one jumble around the other.
explanation.definitionFit: The clavicle is the bone most often fractured in falls.

clue.text: He suffered spirited exhortations to mend his ways

definitions.text: He suffered spirited exhortations to mend his ways

parts.words: He suffered spirited exhortations to mend his ways
parts.note: spirited means delivered by ghosts: the Dickens miser visited by three spirits on Christmas Eve who urge him to reform

explanation.walkthrough: 'spirited' seems to mean lively, but the exhortations come from spirits in A Christmas Carol.
explanation.definitionFit: The miser of Dickens's story is haunted by ghosts who persuade him to change.

clue.text: Having no illusions about a Moslem's credit, say

parts.note: re means about or concerning
Ali is a common Muslim name, so Ali's is a Moslem's

indicators.note: say signals that the word for credit is given by how it sounds

parts.note: tick is British slang for credit, as in buying on tick

explanation.surface: A clear-eyed view of a Muslim man's borrowing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on tick' is British slang for buying on credit; TICK sounds like TIC ('say').
explanation.definitionFit: A realistic person sees things as they are, free of illusions.

clue.text: Couturier taking a scholar 'to a museum display

parts.note: Christian Dior was a French fashion designer
MA, a Master of Arts, is a scholar

explanation.surface: A fashion designer brings an academic to see an exhibit.
explanation.definitionFit: A diorama is a three-dimensional scene set up as an exhibit in a museum.

clue.text: Toad, say, reportedly travelled on the back of a pig

indicators.note: on the back of puts the pig at the rear of the word
reportedly says the word for travelled is heard, not spelt

parts.note: rode means travelled on horseback or in a vehicle
a hog is a pig

explanation.surface: A toad, it is said, went riding on a pig's back.
explanation.walkthrough: Mr Toad of The Wind in the Willows is a reckless motorist, hence the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A selfish, reckless driver is a road hog, and Mr Toad is the classic fictional one.

clue.text: A couple of kings are more dignified

parts.note: GR is Georgius Rex, King George
the couple is joined by the word and
ER is Edwardus Rex, King Edward

explanation.surface: Two monarchs seem more stately than one.
explanation.walkthrough: Two kings joined: GR and ER, the royal cyphers of a George and an Edward.
explanation.definitionFit: Grander means more imposing or stately, so more dignified.

clue.text: Call for prayer

definitions.meaning: to call for them and fetch them
a short liturgical prayer for a particular day

explanation.definitionFit: The word means to fetch someone and also names a short set prayer in church services.

clue.text: Thwarted when cheques are marked thus?

definitions.meaning: two parallel lines across a cheque mean it can only be paid into a bank account

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a cheque with two lines drawn across it can only be paid into an account.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is foiled, the other the pair of lines drawn on a cheque to restrict payment.

clue.text: Big picture in which gourmet sacrifices 23

indicators.note: sacrifices says the gourmet gives up part of himself

parts.note: an epicure is a lover of fine food
23 refers to the clue answer 'Don, possibly'; the Ure is one such in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A grand film in which a foodie gives something up.
explanation.walkthrough: EPICURE loses URE ('sacrifices'), a Yorkshire waterway like the Don of 23.
explanation.definitionFit: An epic is a large-scale film, a blockbuster.

clue.text: Starchy cereal makes a good meal, in part

indicators.note: in part says only a portion of the words, read straight through, is wanted

explanation.surface: A starchy grain makes a decent meal in some measure.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across MAKES A GOOD.
explanation.definitionFit: Sago is the starch from palm pith, used as a pudding grain.

clue.text: Don, possibly, from royal town in Bucks

parts.note: R, as in rex or regina, abbreviates royal
Iver is a village in Buckinghamshire, an English county

explanation.surface: A university don perhaps hails from a regal place in Buckinghamshire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don' looks like a lecturer but is the Don, a river in Yorkshire. Bucks is Buckinghamshire, a county west of London.
explanation.definitionFit: The Don is a watercourse in northern England, one example of the type.

clue.text: Wake old poet right away

indicators.note: away says the letter for right is sent off from the poet's name

parts.note: Virgil was the Roman poet of the Aeneid

explanation.surface: Rouse the ancient bard and send him off.
explanation.walkthrough: VIRGIL with R taken 'away'.
explanation.definitionFit: A wake is a watch kept over the dead, a vigil.

clue.text: Fake diamond taken from plant

indicators.note: taken from says the gem word is removed from the plant

parts.note: the shamrock is a clover-like plant
rock is slang for a diamond

explanation.surface: A false gem removed from a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: SHAMROCK with ROCK 'taken from' it.
explanation.definitionFit: A sham is a counterfeit or pretence.

clue.text: Nick is chapel, we presume

definitions.meaning: a chapel, we presume, is no church: the negative followed by CH, the abbreviation for church

explanation.walkthrough: The second part is a cryptic reading: a chapel is 'not CH', CH being church.
explanation.definitionFit: A notch is a small V-shaped cut, the same as a nick.

clue.text: Ousted theologian receiving physicist on island

indicators.note: receiving says the theologian's letters take the other pieces inside them

parts.note: DD, Doctor of Divinity, is a theologian

indicators.note: on in an across clue puts the physicist after the island

parts.note: Sir Oliver Lodge was a British physicist and radio pioneer

explanation.surface: A churchman takes in a scientist on an island and is then thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' in an across clue puts the physicist after the island; 'receiving' has the theologian's letters take both inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To be dislodged is to be removed or forced out of position.

clue.text: University sportsman taking two Conservatives round radio village

indicators.note: round says the two party pieces go around the village

parts.note: C abbreviates Conservative
blue is the colour of the Conservative party, so a Tory is a blue
Ambridge is the village of the BBC radio soap The Archers

explanation.surface: A college athlete brings two Tories along to a fictional radio village.
explanation.walkthrough: The Archers is a long-running BBC radio soap set in Ambridge. C and BLUE go 'round' it.
explanation.definitionFit: A Blue is a sportsperson who has represented Oxford or Cambridge against the other, here the Cambridge one.
